Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Story: Toshiba HDD Capacity Doubling: STX/WDC −10%—Scope and Timeline. Related tickers: STX, WDC, TER, IMOS.

This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: STX and WDC each fell ~10% on a Nikkei report of Toshiba doubling AI data-center HDD capacity with a $380M Philippines investment, but no details on timeline, customer commitments, or whether TER's +8% gain is causally linked to HDD test demand are in the notes.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- What capacity expansion timeline and customer commitments did the Nikkei October 2 2026 report specify for Toshiba's planned doubling of AI data-center hard-disk-drive production in the Philippines?
- Did Seagate or Western Digital management or any sell-side analyst comment on the competitive threat from Toshiba's HDD expansion in the October 2–5 2026 window?
- Is Teradyne's 8% gain on October 2 2026 linked by analysts to HDD test-equipment demand from Toshiba's Philippine expansion or to a separate AI memory-test catalyst?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

RULES

content:
## Toshiba HDD expansion `[Scope and timeline]`
- Toshiba plans to invest approximately **¥60 billion ($380 million)** in its Philippines facilities to **double production capacity for AI-data-center HDDs by fiscal 2027**, measured against fiscal 2025 capacity; the investment is its first major HDD-related investment in about five years. (Nikkei, Oct. 2, 2026; Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026)
- The new production lines are designed for HDDs with **up to 40% higher per-drive capacity**; Toshiba plans **30TB-class drives in 2027**, mass production of **65TB-class drives around 2030**, and eventually **100TB-class products**. (Nikkei, Oct. 2, 2026; Tom’s Hardware, Oct. 2, 2026)
- Toshiba is targeting an increase in its HDD market share measured by storage capacity from **just over 10% to approximately 30% over the medium term**. (Nikkei, Oct. 2, 2026)
- Toshiba’s Philippine expansion is centered on its **Laguna Technopark** facility and includes additional lines for nearline HDD assembly; some equipment is already installed and first drives from the expanded lines have reportedly begun shipping. [report] (Tom’s Hardware, Oct. 2, 2026; HWBusters, Oct. 3, 2026)
- The reports specify a **fiscal-2027 completion target**, but do not give an exact completion month, production-unit target, or named customer contracts. (Nikkei, Oct. 2, 2026; AI Weekly, Oct. 4, 2026)
- The reported plan does not identify named cloud or AI-data-center customers, customer volume commitments, or customer contract dates; a separate report said the added factory could be relevant to buyers negotiating contracts for **2029 or 2031** shipments. [report] (AI Weekly, Oct. 4, 2026; FinanceFeeds, Oct. 3, 2026)
- Toshiba’s production-line expansion is expected to support drives with increased storage density, while additional investment is planned for **65TB-class production in 2030** and later **100TB-class drives**. (Nikkei, Oct. 2, 2026; Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026)

## STX — Seagate Technology `[Stock move and analyst comments]`
- **STX fell 13% on Oct. 2, 2026**, according to one market report; another report cited an approximately **10%** decline, while a separate price report cited a **14.6%** close. (Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026; FinanceFeeds, Oct. 3, 2026; Startup Fortune, Oct. 3, 2026)
- **Citi analyst Asiya Merchant** said Toshiba’s expansion may have a limited effect on global HDD supply because Toshiba relies on outside suppliers for key components including **media and recording heads**; those suppliers would also need to expand capacity. (Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026)
- **Morgan Stanley** said the HDD supply-demand gap through **2028** remains wider than the capacity addition implied by Toshiba’s plan and characterized the selloff as a buying opportunity; the available report excerpt does not state a rating or price target. [report] (Gate, Oct. 3, 2026)
- **Rosenblatt** described Toshiba’s plan as an attempt to reclaim market share rather than immediately reach the **30%** target, while identifying potential contract risk for supply agreements extending into **2029–2031**; the available report excerpt does not state a rating or price target. [report] (Gate, Oct. 3, 2026)
- Citi, Morgan Stanley, and Rosenblatt are the named firms commenting in the available Oct. 2–5 reports; no specific STX rating change or price-target change is stated in those reports. (Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026; Gate, Oct. 3, 2026)

## WDC — Western Digital `[Stock move and analyst comments]`
- **WDC fell 12% on Oct. 2, 2026**, according to one market report; other reports cited declines of approximately **7%**, **10%**, and **13.5%**. (Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026; Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026; FinanceFeeds, Oct. 3, 2026; Startup Fortune, Oct. 3, 2026)
- **Citi analyst Asiya Merchant** said the effect of Toshiba’s expansion on global HDD availability could be limited because Toshiba does not produce all key components internally and depends on external suppliers for media and heads. (Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026)
- **Morgan Stanley** said capacity additions from Toshiba would not close the HDD supply-demand gap through **2028** and viewed the selloff as a buying opportunity; the available report excerpt does not state a rating or price target. [report] (Gate, Oct. 3, 2026)
- **Rosenblatt** said Toshiba’s plan represented a medium-term share-recapture effort and flagged supply-contract risk in **2029–2031**; the available report excerpt does not state a rating or price target. [report] (Gate, Oct. 3, 2026)
- No named Seagate or Western Digital executive comment, specific WDC rating change, or WDC price-target change is stated in the available Oct. 2–5 reports. (Investing.com, Oct. 2, 2026; Gate, Oct. 3, 2026)

## TER — Teradyne `[Catalyst attribution]`
- **TER rose 8% on Oct. 2, 2026**, according to the premise of the market brief, but the available reports do not link that move to Toshiba’s Philippines HDD expansion.
- The available reports do not identify a named analyst, rating, price target, or dated research note attributing TER’s Oct. 2 gain to HDD test-equipment demand from Toshiba.
- The available reports also do not provide a named analyst attribution linking TER’s gain to a separate AI-memory-test catalyst.

## IMOS — ChipMOS Technologies `[Related ticker]`
- No Oct. 2–5, 2026 report in the available results gives **IMOS** a stock move, analyst note, rating, price target, or causal connection to Toshiba’s Philippines HDD expansion.
